purpose: Map executable valuation Python modules to formula families, authoritative sources, modeling limits, and tests. This registry is a control surface: if a valuation script is not covered here, it should not be treated as a high-confidence executable valuation algorithm.

status_definitions.standard_formula: Formula is a widely accepted finance/accounting formula with direct source support. Inputs can still be uncertain.
status_definitions.standard_with_modeling_judgment: Formula family is standard, but peer selection, normalization, probabilities, recovery rates, or scenario weights materially affect correctness.
status_definitions.heuristic_helper: Useful deterministic helper or simplified economics bridge. It must not be presented as a complete valuation model without additional source-backed assumptions.
status_definitions.infrastructure: No valuation formula. The module packages, routes, validates, or transports inputs/results.

formulas.formula: per_share_value = value / shares_outstanding
formulas.notes: General per-share conversion arithmetic.

formulas.formula: equity_value = enterprise_value - net_debt - minority_interest + non_operating_assets
formulas.notes: Enterprise-to-equity bridge; input definitions must be consistent.

limitations: Infrastructure helpers do not validate whether enterprise value inputs are correctly sourced.
Schema container only; no valuation mathematics.
Execution orchestration only; correctness depends on routed model inputs and called model modules.

formulas.formula: owner_earnings = net_income + depreciation_amortization - maintenance_capex - required_working_capital_increase
formulas.notes: Simplified owner-earnings implementation; other non-cash charges must be included in inputs if material.

formulas.formula: PV = sum(CF_t / (1 + r)^t); equity_value = PV_forecast + PV_terminal - net_debt
formulas.notes: Standard DCF present value mechanics.

formulas.formula: terminal_value = final_cash_flow * (1 + g) / (r - g)
formulas.notes: Requires r > g and a sustainable stable-growth assumption.

limitations: Maintenance capex and working capital needs are judgmental assumptions.
Terminal growth must be sustainable and below discount rate.

formulas.formula: market_implied_ev = market_cap + net_debt
formulas.notes: Market-implied enterprise value bridge.

formulas.formula: Solve g where target_EV = sum(FCF_0 * (1 + g)^t / (1 + r)^t) + TV / (1 + r)^n
formulas.notes: Bisection solver is deterministic; economic interpretation depends on base FCF quality.

formulas.formula: Revenue_t = Revenue_0 * (1 + growth)^t; FCF_t = Revenue_t * target_FCF_margin
formulas.notes: Simplified revenue-to-FCF bridge for implied-expectation checks.

limitations: Does not model taxes, reinvestment, dilution, or explicit margin ramps unless encoded in inputs.
Same-day market price is required for current-price reverse DCF.

formulas.formula: EPV_enterprise_value = normalized_EBIT * (1 - tax_rate) / WACC
formulas.notes: No-growth perpetuity using normalized after-tax operating earnings.

formulas.formula: EPV_equity_value = EPV_enterprise_value - net_debt; franchise_value = DCF_value - EPV_value
formulas.notes: Used as a no-growth / franchise-value cross-check.

limitations: Normalized EBIT and maintenance economics are judgmental.
Not suitable when current earnings are structurally unrepresentative.

formulas.formula: residual_income = net_income - cost_of_equity * beginning_book_value
formulas.notes: Residual income / EVA-style equity valuation logic.

formulas.formula: equity_value = current_book_value + sum(RI_t / (1 + cost_of_equity)^t)
formulas.notes: Appropriate when book value and ROE economics are meaningful.

formulas.formula: P/B = (ROE - g) / (cost_of_equity - g)
formulas.notes: Fundamental P/B support formula; requires sustainable ROE, growth, and cost of equity.

limitations: Book value must be economically meaningful.
Cost of equity and residual income forecasts must be source-backed assumptions.

formulas.formula: value = D1 / (r - g); implied_g = r - D1 / price
formulas.notes: Stable-growth dividend discount model.

formulas.formula: value = PV(explicit dividends) + PV(terminal dividend value)
formulas.notes: Two-stage DDM for temporary high growth followed by stable growth.

formulas.formula: yield = dividend / price; payout = dividend / earnings; coverage = FCFE / dividends; yield_band_value = dividend / target_yield
formulas.notes: Dividend safety and yield-band helpers.

limitations: Use as valuation anchor only when dividends approximate sustainable distributable cash flow.
Requires r > g.

formulas.formula: NAV = fair_value_assets - fair_value_liabilities; NAV_per_share = NAV / shares; discount_to_NAV = (NAV_per_share - price) / NAV_per_share
formulas.notes: Asset-minus-liabilities framework; fair value inputs must be independently sourced.

limitations: Asset and liability fair values are the hard part; stale appraisals or book values reduce confidence.

formulas.formula: segment_value = metric * multiple or explicit_value; SOTP_EV = sum(segment_values) - corporate_cost_value; equity_value = EV - net_debt - minority_interest + non_operating_assets
formulas.notes: SOTP is a standard decomposition framework; segment multiples and explicit values require separate support.

limitations: Segment metrics, ownership, and multiple selection dominate output reliability.
Holding-company discounts are assumptions, not formula facts.

formulas.formula: peer_multiple = median or trimmed median of comparable multiples; EV = metric * multiple; equity_value = EV - net_debt - minority_interest + non_operating_assets
formulas.notes: Comparable valuation is a market-based cross-check, not standalone intrinsic value.

limitations: Peer selection, multiple normalization, and quality adjustments are judgmental and must be source-backed.
Do not let a single multiple drive final conclusion.

formulas.formula: recoverable_assets = carrying_value * recovery_rate; settled_claims = claim_value * settlement_rate; liquidation_equity = recoveries - claims - liquidation_costs
formulas.notes: Balance-sheet recovery arithmetic; recovery rates are scenario assumptions.

limitations: Recovery and settlement rates require hard evidence or conservative assumptions.
Legal priority, off-balance-sheet claims, and liquidation costs can dominate results.

formulas.formula: rNPV_asset = PV(success_cash_flows) * probability_of_success - PV(development_costs); portfolio_rNPV = sum(asset_rNPV) + net_cash - corporate_overhead_PV
formulas.notes: Probability-adjusted NPV for biotech/pharma assets.

formulas.formula: product_FCF = peak_sales * FCF_margin with ramp, plateau, and decline schedule
formulas.notes: Deterministic helper for a simplified product cash-flow curve.

limitations: Probability of success, launch timing, peak sales, patent life, and development costs are high-sensitivity assumptions.
Pipeline costs may need stage-specific probability treatment beyond this simplified helper.

formulas.formula: property_value = NOI / cap_rate; equity_value = EV - net_debt - minority_interest + non_operating_assets
formulas.notes: NOI capitalization is a standard real estate valuation shorthand; cap rate source matters.

formulas.formula: value = AFFO * multiple; AFFO_yield = AFFO / equity_market_cap; distribution_coverage = AFFO / distributions
formulas.notes: Nareit defines FFO; AFFO is company/analyst adjusted and must be reconciled.

limitations: AFFO is not uniformly defined across companies.
Cap rates, NOI adjustments, and leverage require market/current property evidence.

formulas.formula: mid_cycle_metric = average(cycle_values); EV = normalized_metric * mid_cycle_multiple; equity_value = EV bridge
formulas.notes: Mid-cycle normalization is a conventional cyclical valuation technique, but cycle selection is judgmental.

formulas.formula: EBITDA = volume * (commodity_price - cash_cost_per_unit) - fixed_costs; drawdown = (normalized_value - stressed_value) / normalized_value
formulas.notes: Commodity scenario arithmetic helper, not a complete reserve/resource valuation.

limitations: Cycle window, normalized multiple, commodity price, cash cost, and fixed-cost assumptions must be externally supported.
Do not present helper output as full intrinsic value without reserves, depletion, capex, and balance sheet checks.

formulas.formula: equity_value = (adjusted_book_value + value_of_new_business + underwriting_value + investment_portfolio_adjustment) * (1 - holding_company_discount)
formulas.notes: Simplified embedded-value-style bridge; not a full MCEV/EEV actuarial model.

formulas.formula: combined_ratio = (incurred_losses + expenses) / earned_premiums; float_cost = -underwriting_profit / average_float; value = book_value * target_P/B
formulas.notes: Insurance operating-quality helpers and book-value valuation support.

limitations: Full insurance valuation needs reserve adequacy, regulatory capital, asset duration, loss development, and line-of-business mix.
Embedded value inputs must come from company disclosures or actuarial source data.

formulas.formula: revenue = funded_customers * ARPU + net_interest_income + crypto_revenue + other_revenue; stream_revenue_t = stream_revenue_{t-1} * (1 + growth) * stress_factor
formulas.notes: Business-driver bridge for fintech/brokerage economics, not an authoritative valuation formula by itself.

formulas.formula: equity_value = revenue * normalized_margin * earnings_multiple - net_debt
formulas.notes: Normalized earnings multiple helper.

limitations: ARPU, funded customers, rate sensitivity, crypto activity, normalized margin, and multiple must be independently sourced.
Use as support for a routed model, not as complete intrinsic value.

formulas.formula: expected_value = sum(value_i * probability_i), with probabilities summing to 1
formulas.notes: Expected-value scenario weighting.

formulas.formula: DCF = sum(CF_t / (1 + r)^t) plus optional Gordon terminal value
formulas.notes: Generic deterministic DCF helper.

limitations: Scenario probabilities and values must have evidence; probabilities must sum to 1.
